author: Edge
text:
Hi Frosty, dont apologise mate. The point I was making was this:

When those kinks of the CP where first made, in order for them to be FL's they needed to touch the blue zone, which they did.

So when we have the clean orders on the retrace we expect them to hit the red kinks and retrace back to a TG. In this case we only get small reactions and they never hit an opposing TG upon returning. Therefore, they are considered ignored. If they retraced to a MPL of the blue zone then blasted through the red areas, they would be considered used up as opposed to ignored.

Cheers

author: Ifmyante
text:
Hi. We often ignore posts in which the attachments haven't been inserted into the text. Be sure to hit the insert button in future

Right, I don't know what instrument this is, so I can only go by your chart.

It seems you thought you had an engulf up, but all you had was an higher high into what looks like a significant set of orders. At the bottom, you also had a pair of lows, which are always screaming to be broken, to take the retail range traders' stops.

Add to that the fact that when you have an engulf up from a demand level, the RT can always diamond down deeper into demand.

There are so many lessons to be learned from this site! You'll need to know them all before you can trade properly. But we're here to help when you get stuck
